methodologyNotes: Covers standalone hunting and target crossbows sold complete (as a bare bow or a manufacturer ready-to-hunt package) at a published US price. Excludes pistol crossbows, air-powered arrow rifles, replacement/upgrade limb kits, and youth toy crossbows. Price is typical US retail or MSRP in USD for the bare bow or the manufacturer's base package. bowType is an enum: 'compound', 'reverse-draw' (reverse-draw compound), or 'recurve'. advertisedSpeedFps is the manufacturer's rated arrow speed in feet per second with the spec-weight arrow (real-world broadhead-tipped hunting speeds run 20-40 FPS lower). drawWeightLbs is peak draw weight in pounds. powerStrokeIn is the power stroke in inches. kineticEnergyFtlbs is rated kinetic energy in foot-pounds; null if not disclosed. cockedWidthIn is axle-to-axle limb width when cocked, in inches. overallLengthIn is overall length in inches. weightLbs is bare-bow weight without accessories in pounds. cockingMechanism is an enum of the standard cocking device: 'rope-sled', 'integrated-crank', or 'integrated-silent-crank'. arrowLengthIn is the manufacturer's spec arrow/bolt length in inches. scopeIncluded is a boolean indicating whether an optical scope ships in the base package.

products.name: TenPoint TRX Ultra
products.priceNote: Manufacturer product page (tenpointcrossbows.com) lists the TRX Ultra package at a price range of "$3,549.99 through $3,649.99" depending on finish (Moss Green / Vektra Clear). Base package price $3,549.99 used.
products.provenance: The TenPoint manufacturer product page (source) confirms model identity as the reverse-draw "TRX Ultra" — distinct from the separate "TRX Ultra Vision" rangefinding-scope variant — and lists its spec table verbatim: 515 fps, 16.25" power stroke, 11.75"/6" uncocked/cocked axle-to-axle width, 29.5" length, 8.4 lbs weight, ACUslide MAXX silent cocking/de-cocking system, included 100-yard EVO-X Marksman Elite scope, and "515 fps / 242 fp ke" with the 410-grain Pro Elite 400 arrow. The same page lists the package price at "$3,549.99 through $3,649.99" by finish (base $3,549.99). Lancaster Archery Supply (corroboration) independently confirms the same model with matching 515 FPS, 29.5" length, 8.4 lbs, and 16.25" power stroke; peak draw weight and spec arrow length are not stated on either page, so both are left null.

products.name: Ravin R10X
products.priceNote: US MSRP $1,899.99 — Ravin's own "Regular Price $1,899.99" listed verbatim on the official R10X Black page (shown against a reconditioned "Special Price $1,359.99"). New-unit street prices at the access date were lower at retailers (Midwest Archery $1,599.00; Wyvern Creations $1,349.99), cited here for context only.
products.provenance: The official Ravin site page "Ravin R10X Black" (ravincrossbows.com, SKU 9-D015) confirmed the exact model and its factory specifications: 420 fps (400 gr.), 156 ft-lbs kinetic energy, 6.8 lbs product weight, 33" length, 12 lbs draw force, a Fully Integrated Silent Cocking System, and a 100-yard illuminated scope in the base package; it lists Ravin's own "Regular Price $1,899.99." Wyvern Creations (SKU R10X, UPC 815942020159) corroborated those figures and additionally states the 6" cocked axle-to-axle width and matching 156 ft-lbs KE. A Midwest Archery listing gave a conflicting kinetic energy (142 ft-lbs) and power stroke (11" vs Wyvern's 10"), so power stroke was left null; the 420 fps rating distinguishes this R10X from the 400 fps R10 and the newer 2026 R10X Pro.

products.name: Excalibur Rev X TD
products.priceNote: Manufacturer page (excaliburcrossbow.com/bows/revx-td) lists "Starting at $1999.99" MSRP. Lancaster Archery Supply lists the RevX TD package street price at $1,899.99. priceUsd uses the $1999.99 manufacturer MSRP.
products.provenance: The Excalibur manufacturer page (excaliburcrossbow.com/bows/revx-td) confirms this is the exact RevX TD takedown model, stating Speed 400 FPS, Overall Length 33", Weight 7.5/9.6 LBS, Draw Effort 16 LBS, Draw Type Integrated Crank (ChargerX), an included Overwatch Illuminated Scope, 16.5" ProFlight arrows, Excalibur's recurve design, and price "Starting at $1999.99". The Lancaster Archery retailer page (Item #1044991, "Excalibur REV-X TD Crossbow Package") corroborates the same model and specs and adds a cocked width of 21", listing a street price of $1,899.99. drawWeightLbs is left null because the 16 lb figure is the crank draw effort (labeled "Draw Effort" by the manufacturer), not the limbs' peak draw weight the methodology requires; power stroke and kinetic energy are not disclosed on either page.

products.name: Barnett Hyper Raptor
products.priceNote: US MSRP $699.99 — listed verbatim as "$699.99" on the Pyramyd AIR product page and matched by Barnett's own store listing (Shopify price 69999 = $699.99, SKU BAR78182). Street/clearance prices run lower (e.g., Lancaster Archery lists $450.00 clearance), but $699.99 is the manufacturer/retailer list price.
products.provenance: Barnett's official product page (SKU BAR78182, "Hyper Raptor™") confirmed the exact model and stated draw weight 214 lbs, power stroke 14", axle-to-axle 7.25" when cocked, 32.5" length, 20" HyperFlite arrows, a Sled Style Rope Cocking Device, and an included 4x36 illuminated scope; its prose gives 410 fps / 142 ft-lbs (an inconsistent spec-table listed 425 fps / 152, which I did not use). Pyramyd AIR corroborated the identical model with matching figures (410 fps, 142 ft-lbs, 214 lb draw, 7.25" cocked, 32.5" overall length, 7.1 lb weight, "Compound Crossbow") and listed the price at $699.99. Bare-bow weight (7.1 lbs) is sourced from Pyramyd since Barnett's spec table omitted weight.

products.name: Killer Instinct Boss 405
products.priceNote: Killer Instinct official store (shop.kicrossbows.com/boss-405-crossbow/) lists the Boss 405 Pro Package at a regular price of $329.99 (currently discounted to a $299.99 sale price). Borkholder Archery corroborates the same $329.99 regular price. Using $329.99 as the typical US retail / MSRP for the base Pro Package (the Boss 405 is sold only as a ready-to-hunt package, no bare-bow option).
products.provenance: The official Killer Instinct manufacturer store page (shop.kicrossbows.com/boss-405-crossbow/) confirmed this exact model — "BOSS 405 CROSSBOW" — with its verbatim SPECS block (SPEED 405 FPS, KINETIC ENERGY 134-FT-LB, WIDTH 14.75" Cocked//18.75" Uncocked, LENGTH 33.5"-36", WEIGHT 6.7-LB, DRAW WT 220-LB, POWER STROKE 13.25") and a regular price of $329.99. Borkholder Archery (retailer) independently corroborated every one of those spec values in a clean specification table and the same $329.99 regular price. Amazon's official Killer Instinct Store listing (Model Number 1104, UPC 859826007423) further confirmed model identity and the included LUMIX 4x32 IR-W scope and Rope Cocker; overallLengthIn was left null because the source states only an adjustable range (33.5"-36"), and arrowLengthIn was left null because the Boss 405 spec block does not state a bolt length.

products.name: Wicked Ridge Commander 400
products.priceNote: US MSRP $599.99 per the official TenPoint/Wicked Ridge product page (listed price "$ 599.99"); corroborated by Lancaster Archery Supply listing the same package at "$599.99".
products.provenance: The official TenPoint/Wicked Ridge product page confirms model identity as the "Wicked Ridge Commander 400" and provides a dedicated Specs table: 400 fps, 190 lb draw weight, 12.5" power stroke, 14.5"/11" uncocked/cocked axle-to-axle width, 35.75" length (w/o foot stirrup), 7.3 lb weight, built-in ACUdraw cocking device, Pro-View 400 lighted scope, and "400 fps / 146 fp ke" with the 410-grain Match 400 arrow — priced at $599.99. Lancaster Archery Supply (Item #1044760) corroborates the same model and price ($599.99), repeating 400 FPS, 11" cocked axle-to-axle, the integrated ACUdraw crank, and the included Pro-View 400 scope; its marketing copy lists 6.3 lb / 36" but I used the manufacturer's official spec-table figures (7.3 lb, 35.75"). Arrow/bolt length is not stated in inches on either page, so arrowLengthIn is null; bowType is compound (forward-draw MDX cam system).

products.name: CenterPoint Wrath 430
products.priceNote: US MSRP $649.99 for the base Wrath 430 with the standard rope sled cocker. Archery Business "Published Specs" lists "MSRP: $649.99" and states "MSRP is $699.99 with the Silent Cranking Device, or $649.99 with the standard sled cocker." Bowhunting.com corroborates: "Price – $649.99" and "The Wrath 430 is priced at $649.99."
products.provenance: Fetched two dated bow-report reviews of the exact base CenterPoint Wrath 430 (bullpup stock, rope sled cocker, $649.99 — explicitly distinguished from the $699.99 Silent Crank/SC variant and the separate inverted-cam Wrath 430X). Archery Business (Dec 13, 2021, Stephen D. Carpenteri) provides a "Published Specs" table confirming Model: Wrath 430 with 200 lb draw, 15 in power stroke, 20 in arrows, 430 fps, 164 ft-lbs, 28.26 in overall length, 9 in cocked / 13 in uncocked axle-to-axle width, 8.3 lb weight, 4x32 illuminated scope provided, "Rope sled cocker included," and "MSRP: $649.99." Bowhunting.com (July 9, 2021, Brodie Swisher) independently corroborates every figure and the $649.99 price; the manufacturer's live product page for the base model now redirects to the 430X and 404s, so these two dated reviews serve as the verbatim sources.

products.name: Mission Sub-1 XR
products.priceNote: Manufacturer product page (missioncrossbows.com/crossbows/sub-1-xr) states verbatim "Starting at $ 2,299.00" for the SUB-1 XR. Lancaster Archery Supply lists the Mission SUB-1 XR Crossbow (with Pro Kit) at $2,299.00, matching. (For historical context, the June 2021 Archery Business review cited the original launch MSRP as $1,899.98 for the package / $1,699 bow-only; the current sourced figure is $2,299.00.)
products.provenance: The Mission Crossbows manufacturer page confirmed the model as the SUB-1 XR and stated its core specs verbatim (Speed Up To 410 FPS, Physical Weight 7.6 LBS, Powerstroke 14.625", Length 30.5", Width axle-to-axle 9.1" cocked) along with the price "Starting at $ 2,299.00". The dated Archery Business review (June 25, 2021) explicitly identifies "Model: Sub-1 XR (Extended Range), Manufacturer: Mission Crossbows (a division of Mathews)" and supplies the published draw weight (250 pounds, 80% let-off) and 19-inch spec arrow length not listed on the manufacturer page, while corroborating the 410 fps speed, 30.5" length, 7.6 lb weight and 9.1" cocked width. Both pages confirm the base/basic package ships with a Hawke illuminated scope and a rope cocker, with the RSD (Removable Silent Draw) silent crank sold separately as an optional accessory — so scopeIncluded=true and the standard cocking device is a rope-sled.
